inspiration: Grey-to-ramp recolour: a neutral sprite takes many tints because its brightness is looked up in a per-tint ramp. The ramp is a short strip per hue, not a full gradient. For armour, a steel or gold finish can come from one grey base sprite plus our own ramps (IsometricWorld.fx PixelShader_Hue; HueData.cs getTextureData).

Two recolour modes: full tint over everything, or tint only the neutral pixels so trim and coloured details survive (IsometricWorld.fx line 92 comment). Strong for armour trim and for hero gear dressing.
A single vertex attribute packs tint index, tint mode, transparency and a no-lighting flag (doc/VertexPositionNormalTextureHue.txt). A shader author can use the packing idea with our own bit layout.

Container gumps as data: each container has a rectangle, a drop sound and an optional item-ID whitelist (containers.cfg). A loot chest that accepts only certain items, with its own drop sound, is a clean loot-ceremony pattern.
Body classes keyed by body ID (bodytable.cfg): equipment, monster, animal, human and sea rows. Gear rules attach to a body class, not to each creature. Relevant to gear dressing and to creature rigs.

Shadow pass with a stencil: an opaque sprite writes one half-transparent dark pixel, and the stencil stops overlaps from darkening twice (IsometricWorld.fx PixelShader_ShadowSet). Good model for ground shadows under our creatures.

Legacy rich-text subset: a few tags (bold, italic, underline, outline, size, alignment), block layout, unknown tags ignored (doc/Html tags supported by UltimaXNA.txt). Fits item descriptions in our HUD.

briefs.label: Neutral-ramp armour finish
briefs.why: Metal reads at 375 wide from one hard highlight band. One grey base sprite plus several ramps gives gold, steel and bronze without redrawing each piece. Signature effect: a bright rim that holds its colour when the piece is hit.
briefs.keep: Brightness of the base pixel picks a column in a per-tint ramp. A partial mode tints only the neutral pixels so trim survives.
briefs.change: Author our own ramps per material with a hard specular band at the top, not a generic tint. Put the tint on a second channel so hit flash does not wipe the highlight. Different ramp count and order per material.

briefs.label: Locked chest with item filter and own drop sound
briefs.why: A chest that accepts only some items reads at a glance: the gump shape says what goes in. A drop sound per container is a cheap loot ceremony.
briefs.keep: Each container is data: size and place on the gump, drop sound, optional whitelist of item IDs.
briefs.change: Give each chest its own silhouette and lid animation. Tie the drop sound to rarity tier, and add a rim glow when a valid item hovers over it. Our item IDs, not theirs.

briefs.label: Body-class gear rule
briefs.why: Gear fits a body class, not a species. A quadruped and a biped can share a gear rule set, so new creatures need no new gear work.
briefs.keep: A table from body ID to class (equipment, monster, animal, human, sea). Gear and rigs key off the class.
briefs.change: Use our own classes: plated biped, armoured quadruped, serpent, winged. Rig rules per class, and a visible silhouette change when gear is worn.

briefs.label: Single-pass ground shadow
briefs.why: Overlapping sprites do not darken twice, so a crowd of creatures stays readable at 375 wide. The soft ground shadow sells weight.
briefs.keep: Stencil gate: one dark half-transparent write per screen pixel for opaque sprites.
briefs.change: A soft oval for bipeds and a wider flat shape for quadrupeds, shaped per creature class rather than one blob.

briefs.label: Tag-subset item text
briefs.why: Short item text with bold stat lines and rarity colour reads on a phone. A tiny tag set is easy for writers.
briefs.keep: A handful of tags, block layout, unknown tags ignored so bad markup never breaks the panel.
briefs.change: Our own tags for rarity and stat lines; no legacy tag names. Colour from our palette.
